entries.title: Connect computers without waiting for Agent setup
entries.body:
Connecting a computer now finishes as soon as its OpenMeld Service is safely
running. Local Agents continue preparing in the background, setup commands stay
fresh while the Connect page is open, and OpenMeld automatically recovers more
stale Service installations without asking the user to diagnose them.

entries.title: Let Center Agent choose the right tools
entries.body:
Center Agent now searches its complete capability catalog itself instead of
having OpenMeld guess a few tools from the wording of each request. The same
approach works across supported models, languages, and paraphrases. A small set
of safe member and Task reads stays ready for immediate use, while writes remain
under the Agent's explicit choice and current-status questions distinguish a
fresh read from older Task history. If a model provider completes a turn with
no answer or action at all, OpenMeld now safely retries once before showing a
failure.

entries.title: Setup now reports the final Service state safely
entries.body:
Computer setup now finishes successfully after OpenMeld Service recovers from
a temporary start delay, and shows the Service as connected even when no local
agents are installed yet. Development, Staging, and Canary setup also stay
isolated from the published OpenMeld Service on the same computer.

entries.title: Setup recovers from interrupted downloads
entries.body:
Computer setup now retries a temporarily interrupted OpenMeld download inside
the same command, instead of making the user copy and run the setup command
again.

entries.title: GLM 5.3 Flash is the new Center Agent default
entries.body:
The Center Agent now runs new turns on GLM 5.3 Flash instead of Grok 4.6.
Organizations that did not pick a specific model follow the default on their
next turn; organizations that explicitly selected a model keep that exact
model, and Grok 4.6 stays selectable.

Center Agent settings now also describes the image path accurately: images use
the dedicated vision model before the selected primary model receives the
description.

OpenCode Agent Profiles also gain the current curated OpenCode Go, free-tier,
and Zen model lineup, including GLM 5.3 Flash on OpenCode Go, with each
model's official reasoning variants.

entries.title: Keep Center Agent actions relevant
entries.body:
Center Agent replies no longer show an unrelated Computer setup, Space, or
Project button merely because the agent checked one of those resources while
working. An action appears only when opening that destination is the useful
next step for the current request.

entries.title: Keep Center Agent requests moving through Computer reconnects
entries.body:
Center Agent requests now recover when the private Computer reconnects while a
turn is being prepared. OpenMeld resumes the same request from durable state
before any model or tool work starts, without repeating completed external
actions. If recovery cannot finish, the request reaches one clear failure
instead of remaining indefinitely active.

entries.title: Read Organization members and Tasks with the Center Agent
entries.body:
The Center Agent can page through Organization members without loading
unrelated Agent Profile readiness, and can read the requester's canonical
OpenMeld Tasks separately from local coding-agent task handles.

entries.title: Stop waiting when Center Agent work has failed
entries.body:
When Center Agent work ends in failure, OpenMeld now reports that same final
outcome in the conversation, progress checks, diagnostics, and the CLI Wake
trace summary. Agents no longer keep waiting, treat a failed turn as an
ordinary reply, or suggest that a failed response is still being published.

entries.title: Keep browser notification setup out of the way
entries.body:
Browser notification setup now disappears completely after permission is
granted, “Not now” is selected, or the new close button is used, so members can
immediately continue setup or use the page underneath it.

entries.title: Keep Center Agent completion times accurate
entries.body:
Center Agent diagnostics now keep the time a task first completed when a final
confirmation is safely replayed. Repeated confirmations no longer make a
completed task look slower than it was.

entries.title: Let Agents reply without a shell approval prompt
entries.body:
Agents can now choose and record a Space reply, final status, or silent outcome
through a dispatch-scoped OpenMeld tool without asking the member to approve an
OpenMeld shell command. This does not relax the Agent Profile's normal Codex
permissions. Multi-paragraph replies also preserve real line breaks, literal
`\n` text, quotes, backslashes, emoji, and shell-like characters without
rewriting the message. The dispatch-scoped CLI remains available as a fallback
and for replies with attachments.

entries.title: Prevent incompatible Local Agent model choices
entries.body:
When a selected Local Agent installation clearly cannot run a model, OpenMeld
now disables that model while an Agent Profile is created or edited. The dialog
explains why and links directly to the Computer where the member can update or
change the installation. Missing compatibility information does not block the
member or make OpenMeld guess. Existing Agents that hit the same problem during
a Wake now get the same direct Computer recovery path.

entries.title: Send and safely retry Center Agent Slack messages
entries.body:
Center Agent can send formatted Slack messages again and retry the same message
when OpenMeld fails while preparing it, before anything reaches Slack.
Genuinely uncertain Slack delivery outcomes remain safely blocked so a retry
cannot create a duplicate.

entries.title: Get browser alerts for important Inbox updates
entries.body:
Members can enable browser notifications for directly addressed messages,
actions, urgent items, and requested work endings. OpenMeld avoids interrupting
the conversation already on screen, checks the latest Inbox state before a
queued alert appears, and keeps failed deliveries retryable across account or
conversation changes, refreshes, busy Inbox pages, and multiple tabs.

entries.title: Keep Codex update guidance tied to its installation
entries.body:
OpenMeld no longer compares the Codex included with the ChatGPT app against the
standalone Codex CLI release. ChatGPT app installations stay under the app's
own update channel, while npm and Homebrew installations continue to use their
matching package channels. Codex usage details also put the overall weekly
limit first and use a lighter circular gauge.

entries.title: Keep disabled local agents out of the way
entries.body:
Local agents that you turn off now stay visually quiet and no longer create a
Computer alert. Installation choices also sit with the local agent's launch
details, and OpenMeld waits for the final result before calling a slow setting
change a failure.

entries.title: Recover transient local sign-in reads
entries.body:
OpenMeld now retries one temporarily unavailable saved sign-in read before it
blocks a command, so a brief local credential-store failure does not
unnecessarily stop Space file work. If the saved sign-in remains unavailable,
OpenMeld keeps the diagnostic reason and sanitized lower-level cause in Agent
View and `--json`, then asks the caller to retry or inspect authentication
status instead of incorrectly claiming that the sign-in is invalid. Unexpected
credential-read exceptions follow the same unavailable path instead of being
silently treated as a missing session. Expired, revoked, mismatched, and
genuinely invalid sessions still fail closed.

entries.title: See which local agent installation OpenMeld uses
entries.body:
Computer details now name the exact local agent installation OpenMeld uses and
show provider limits in compact circular cards. Choosing another installation
requires confirmation, stays readable on smaller screens, and no longer shows
a timeout when the computer completed the change.

entries.title: Keep Codex permissions stable during background checks
entries.body:
OpenMeld no longer changes a Codex conversation's approval or sandbox settings
while checking it in the background or recovering an interrupted task. Your
selected Agent Controller Permission Mode now remains in effect for later work.

entries.title: Recover a Mac with a fresh setup command
entries.body:
Fresh setup commands on supported Macs now use the normal macOS Keychain
without requiring a restricted app entitlement. If Keychain is temporarily
unavailable or does not answer within five seconds, OpenMeld stops waiting,
clearly warns the user, keeps the session in private local storage, and finishes
reconnecting the computer. It does not keep retrying Keychain in the same
process. A later successful setup or login automatically moves the session back
to Keychain. OpenMeld Service also reuses its loaded session instead of
repeatedly querying secure storage while it is running.

entries.title: Stop background Keychain authorization windows
entries.body:
OpenMeld no longer opens macOS Keychain password dialogs while local agents are
working in the background or while setup is recovering the computer. Normal
Keychain access stays silent. If macOS requires approval, OpenMeld stops the
Keychain operation immediately, uses its protected local fallback during setup,
and leaves no waiting helper or orphaned password window behind. Developer and
npm CLI paths also stop immediately instead of launching macOS's interactive
`security` tool, so parallel local work cannot queue repeated password dialogs.

entries.title: Collapse sidebar groups when you need more room
entries.body:
The main sidebar now groups People, Agents, and Computers under Team and lets
you collapse Work, Team, and Resources. OpenMeld remembers those choices as you
move between pages, while compact sidebars keep every destination available.

entries.title: Help the Center Agent find the right capability
entries.body:
The Center Agent now loads a small set of tools relevant to each request and
searches the same organized catalog before treating a hidden tool as missing.
This also lets a verified member ask from any current Slack conversation to
privately invite named teammates, while exact directory matching and Core
authorization keep every invitation scoped to the requested people.

entries.title: More reliable Slack onboarding
entries.body:
OpenMeld now keeps Slack setup and welcome delivery recoverable, avoids sending
the same welcome twice, respects the Organization's working language, and only
lets a verified member invite exact Slack teammates through Core-bound private
delivery.

entries.title: Open exact Slack messages from Inbox
entries.body:
Inbox now links Center Agent Slack updates to the exact Slack message. Opening
the link marks the OpenMeld item read, and temporary Slack permalink failures
are retried without creating duplicate Inbox items. Existing Slack items are
upgraded in place without resetting their read, action, or dismissal state.
Tabs left open during the rollout keep the prior Center Agent destination until
they reload the current Web client.

entries.title: Publish only to verified Slack threads
entries.body:
Center Agent thread replies now require an exact Slack message link from the
request or the Slack evidence it just read. OpenMeld verifies that link against
the connected workspace before publishing, so an invented channel or timestamp
cannot redirect the reply.

entries.title: Review and save Profile Report updates
entries.body:
Pending Profile Report updates now explain that they need to be reviewed and
saved. The existing **Save changes** action accepts the visible update even when
no text edit is needed, then clears the matching Inbox action.

entries.title: See computers and connected accounts in People
entries.body:
Human Profile cards now show clear Computer status, existing Profile Reports,
and connected Slack, Lark, or Feishu accounts without exposing internal profile
handles or vague activity labels. Members can complete missing setup from their
own card, disconnect a wrong account, and securely move a provider account to
the right OpenMeld profile after proving control in that channel.

entries.title: See the same Computer status everywhere
entries.body:
Computer cards, detail pages, and navigation now use the same status and
attention color. An available update stays amber everywhere, while required
repairs stay red and Computer details keep one clear OpenMeld Service action.

entries.title: Understand every organization computer
entries.body:
The Home directory now includes every computer shared with the Organization,
even when it has no Agent Profile. Members can also ask the Center Agent or
their own local agent about computers: the Center Agent receives model-safe
owner diagnostics only in the member's private conversation, local agents can
read the authenticated user's complete CLI inventory, and teammate lookups stay
limited to the same safe summary shown in the Organization directory.

entries.title: Use the current Service's controls
entries.body:
Computer controls now follow the newest OpenMeld Service session for that
device and lane. An older reconnecting session can no longer make file access,
folder selection, Project controls, or local Agent controls appear available
when the current Service does not support them.

entries.title: A shared Changelog workflow for coding agents
entries.body:
OpenMeld contributors can record, validate, publish, and historically backfill
product changes through one Git-backed workflow that works across coding
agents.

entries.title: Ask the Center Agent what changed in OpenMeld
entries.body:
Organization members can ask the Center Agent what is new in OpenMeld and get
an answer grounded in the official published Changelog across Web, Slack, and
other supported Channels.

entries.title: Read official OpenMeld updates on the Web
entries.body:
Anyone can read the official OpenMeld Changelog at a public Web page, with
clear publication dates, release names, product areas, and older-update
pagination backed by the same GitHub record used by the Center Agent.
